macro.regime: Hot jobs meet a hawkish Fed and an AI-capex political shock -- two-way whipsaw, oversold bounce
macro.narrative: Friday's partial recovery (S&P +0.31%, Nasdaq +1.09%, VIX -9% to 25.64) came on the same day as a jobs report that should have been unambiguously hawkish -- October nonfarm payrolls smashed consensus at +165K (vs 65K expected), unemployment fell to 4.1% (vs 4.2% expected), and average hourly earnings rose 3.1% y/y (vs 2.9% expected) -- yet equities, led by a chip-sector bounce (AMD +11-13%, Nvidia +2.8-6.4%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +4.4-6.5%), shrugged it off even as CME-implied December-hike odds jumped from the mid-60s/low-70s pre-print into the high-70s/~80% post-print. That resilience looks more like an oversold bounce than conviction: CNN's Fear & Greed Index sits at Extreme Fear (~20-23), the McClellan Oscillator printed a -111.5 washout reading, and the AI-capex political backlash that triggered Thursday's -4.36%/-5.52% rout has broadened well beyond Texas's governor-elect -- Georgia's and Ohio's governors-elect and Loudoun County, VA have all moved on data-center moratoriums, with UBS estimating roughly 30% (and Goldman as much as 45%) of 2028 US data-center capacity now at risk -- even as hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Oracle) have not yet cut 2026 capex guidance. Credit stress remains real but so far idiosyncratic rather than systemic: CoreWeave's bond yield is still above 16% and its 5-year CDS eased only modestly Friday (to ~1,155bp from ~1,289bp Thursday), while the broad ICE BofA US HY OAS sits at 348bp (as of Nov 5), below the cycle's 354bp high rather than accelerating into it. The Bank of England added to a globally synchronized hawkish tilt, hiking to 4.00% Wednesday (8-1, with the lone dissenter wanting 50bp) on an inflation path it sees reaching roughly 5% by Q2 2027, driven by Middle-East-linked energy costs rather than a domestic wage spiral. The single highest-impact date on the near-term calendar is Tuesday Nov 10, when China's rare-earth export-control truce expires with no renewal notice yet published -- a binary catalyst for the MP/Lynas/USA Rare Earth/Energy Fuels basket against the Chinese-incumbent 6680.HK, complicated by a fresh political overhang as incoming Democratic committees open 'subpoena season' on roughly $40B of Trump-era critical-minerals deals, including MP's own government equity stake.

rareEarthCalls.name: MP Materials Corp

Stock still highly volatile intraday (11/6 range $32.07-$36.65) reflecting both the earnings beat and the binary China-policy overhang

rareEarthCalls.name: Lynas Rare Earths Ltd
